title: Opinion verbs and mood: who believes what

sections.content: You know *creo que* + indicative and *no creo que* + subjunctive from B1 Unit 7. When someone believes a claim is true, the verb after *que* is in the indicative. When they do not believe it, the verb after *que* is in the subjunctive. Historians disagree about populism, so both forms appear: *algunos historiadores creen que…; otros no creen que…*.

items.spanish: Algunos historiadores creen que estos movimientos dieron voz a los pobres.
items.english: Some historians believe that these movements gave a voice to the poor.

items.spanish: Otros no creen que el vínculo directo sea bueno para la democracia.
items.english: Others do not believe that the direct link is good for democracy.

items.spanish: Algunos no creen que un sindicato controlado por el Estado pueda defender a los trabajadores.
items.english: Some do not believe that a union controlled by the state can defend the workers.

items.spanish: Muchos creen que la participación del pueblo era real.
items.english: Many believe that the participation of the people was real.

sections.content: The subjunctive shows that the speaker does not accept the idea as a fact (*sea*, *pueda*, *tenga*). The same rule works with *no pensar que* and *no opinar que*. Add the person who holds the view: *algunos historiadores*, *otros*, *según ellos*.
